finding.claim: The authenticated identity is taken directly from a client-supplied HTTP header (X-Session-User-Verified). Nothing in the code authenticates the request or strips the header, so any caller can impersonate any user named in a resource's grants. Impact is unauthorized deletion and renaming of files. This is exploitable unless a trusted front proxy overwrites or strips the header, which is not visible in this code.
finding.source: Request header X-Session-User-Verified, set to any value by the client
finding.sink: ensure_allowed/is_allowed authorization checks guarding `del STORE[fid]` (views.py:18) and `f["name"] = ...` (views.py:27)

trace.note: g.user = request.headers.get('X-Session-User-Verified') with no signature, session or token verification
is_allowed only checks action in resource grants for the supplied user string, so a spoofed owner name passes
rename_file uses the same spoofed g.user for the write check
attacker-controlled name written to the file

finding.guards_checked: Searched for authentication middleware, session validation, header stripping and an HMAC/signature check; none exist in the two files. The ACL check in acl.py is sound given a trusted user value but is bypassed when the user value is forged. An unauthenticated request yields g.user=None and is denied, but any non-empty forged name is accepted. A reverse proxy outside this repo could mitigate this; it is unverified.

verdict.guard_found: ensure_allowed (acl.py:8-10, aborts 403) and is_allowed (acl.py:4-5, checked at views.py:25) are correctly used, but they only compare the unauthenticated header value against the grants. There is no authentication, header stripping or signature check in the repo.
verdict.reason: views.py:11 trusts the client-supplied X-Session-User-Verified header as g.user, and acl.py:5 only checks that string against grants, so any caller who sends a granted user's name passes the checks before `del STORE[fid]` (views.py:18) and the rename at views.py:27. A trusted front proxy that strips or overwrites the header could mitigate this, but none is visible in the repo.
